thread:
Oncall Bot: ALERT: pod redwood-runtime-3 on gpu-cluster-a experiencing repeated OOMs and CUDA_ERROR_LAUNCH failures. avg mem growth over 24h: +12%/day -> potential kv-cache/paged-attn leak. incident id: INC-3309 :rotating_light:
Kai H.: seeing the same on prom: kv_cache_fragmentation_ratio spiking on node gpu-a-07, eviction rate low. kernel logs show 'OOM killer invoked' at 23:12 UTC.
Renee L.: confirmed container restarts on that node, 3 restarts in last 10m. stack traces show majority in attention_paging allocator path.
Samir P.: working on isolating workload — which model families are on that pool?
Kai H.: mostly long-context chat models (redwood-extended-13b variants) with paging enabled. batch sizes ~8.
Jae M.: copying recent kube events ->
```
Kube: Warning  OOMKilled  3m (x3 over 10m)  kubelet, gpu-a-07  container redwood-runtime OOMKilled
Runtime: [cudaErrorLaunchFailure] at attention_paged.cu:421
```
Samir P.: quick mitigation idea: temporarily disable attention paging on that node class or fallback to non-paged kernels for long contexts. can we toggle via env and rollout?
Renee L.: we can set ENV REDWOOD_PAGING=off and restart runtime pods on the affected node pool. risk: increased steady-state memory usage, but should avoid fragmentation-driven OOM spiral.
Kai H.: I'm going to cordon gpu-a-07, drain non-critical pods, and redeploy with paging off to the drained set. doing a canary on one pod first.
Oncall Bot: NOTE: paging disabled flag applied to deployment redwood-runtime-longctx-canary by Kai H. at 23:20 UTC.
Renee L.: canary started. watching mem usage. if stable for 5m, we roll to the rest.
Kai H.: canary looks stable for 6m, mem plateaued instead of creeping. starting rolling restart across pool with small maxUnavailable.
Samir P.: adding immediate transient mitigations: reduce max_batch_tokens to 512 and lower concurrency to 2 for long-context routes. snippet to patch k8s:
```
kubectl -n inference set env deploy/redwood-runtime REDWOOD_PAGING=off REDWOOD_MAX_BATCH_TOKENS=512 REDWOOD_MAX_CONCURRENCY=2
```
Jae M.: running that now.
Kai H.: note: we saw two containers show cuda driver complaint before restart: "CUDA_ERROR_LAUNCH_FAILURE" then node-level driver log shows GPU reset. may need infra restart if persistence continues.
infra-bot: Alert: nvidia-driver resets detected on gpu-a-07 (3 resets / 10m). Scheduling node reboot hold.
Renee L.: customer impact check — any 5xx spike on hosted API?
Samir P.: yes small spike on chat/generate: errors up from baseline 0.2% to 2.1% for the last 15m, mainly timeouts and 502 from runtime pod restarts. estimated impacted requests ~650/min.
Kai H.: posting incident note to #incidents and paging CS for customer outreach.
Oncall Bot: INCIDENT NOTE: assigned eng-runtime oncall @Kai H., @Renee L., @Samir P.
Renee L.: rolling restart complete across pool. memory growth stopped on those nodes. node-level driver resets persist on gpu-a-07.
Jae M.: taking gpu-a-07 OOB: cordon + reboot now, moving remaining pods off.
infra-bot: Node gpu-a-07 reboot scheduled and performed at 23:41 UTC. driver resets cleared.
Samir P.: follow-up: we saw fragmentation metric (kv_paged_free_fragmentation_pct) high ~72% prior to workaround. after disabling paging and rolling restarts it's down to ~28% on affected nodes.
Kai H.: plan for mitigation checklist:
- short-term: keep paging off for long-context pool until we push allocator patch
- medium: land allocator compaction pass that runs on warmup or periodically (kv-slab defrag)
- long-term: add heuristics to increase eviction aggressiveness when fragmentation crosses threshold
Renee L.: created ticket INFRA-4543 to schedule a compaction job and add observability alerts for fragmentation ratio at 50%+
Samir P.: also creating a quick runtime hotfix: bump kv-evict-window from 60s->15s and enable slab-scan during low traffic. prototype code snippet in review.
Kai H.: handoff to next oncall @Jae M. — leaving paging disabled and compaction job scheduled, ticket INFRA-4543 in backlog with priority P1, customer support pinged for impacted customers and CS outreach draft sent.
Jae M.: ack. will monitor for 2h, keep paging off and watch eviction and fragmentation metrics. will escalate if fragmentation increases or OOMs reappear.
Renee L.: FYI, postmortem owners: Kai H. + Samir P. to write incident blameless postmortem, due EOD tomorrow. include timeline, mitigations, and rollout plan for allocator change.
Oncall Bot: HANDOFF: incident INC-3309 now in monitoring state; oncall: Jae M.; next follow-up due 02:00 UTC.
Samir P.: one more note — we should consider an experimental mode where attention paging stays enabled but we force periodic kv cache compaction during low QPS windows. logged as design note in INFRA-4543. :memo:
Kai H.: thanks team. leaving traces/commands we used in the incident channel for runbook updates.
Jae M.: copying runbook entries and adding a new checklist item: 'If fragmentation > 60% and OOMs occur: disable paging, reduce batch size, cordon node, reboot if driver resets'.
Renee L.: closing thread for now, will reopen if flares. :white_check_mark:
